'''''Euphorbia helioscopia''''', the '''sun spurge''' or '''madwoman's milk''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Euphorbia helioscopia (Madwoman's Milk) - Practical Plants |url=https://practicalplants.org/wiki/euphorbia_helioscopia/ |access-date=2024-03-28 |website=practicalplants.org |language=en}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family [[Euphorbiaceae]]. It is a herbaceous [[annual plant]], native to most of [[Europe]], northern [[Africa]], and eastward through most of [[Asia]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 14 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=flora>''Flora Europaea'': [http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Euphorbia+&SPECIES_XREF=helioscopia&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Euphorbia helioscopia'']</ref><ref name=blamey>Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref>

Additional folk names include '''wart spurge''', '''summer spurge''', '''umbrella milkweed''', and '''wolf's-milk'''. <ref name=malta>Malta Wild Plants [http://www.maltawildplants.com/EUPH/Euphorbia_helioscopia.html ''Euphorbia helioscopia''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070807031006/http://www.maltawildplants.com/EUPH/Euphorbia_helioscopia.html |date=2007-08-07 }}</ref><ref>{{GBIF|id=3066367|taxon=''Euphorbia helioscopia''|access-date=4 December 2022}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Euphorbia helioscopia'' is an [[annual plant]] growing in [[arable land]] and [[disturbed ground]]. It grows to 10–50 cm tall, with a single, erect, hairless stem, branching toward the top. The [[leaf|leaves]] are oval, broadest near the tip, 1.5–3 cm long, with a finely toothed margin. The [[flower]]s are small, yellow-green, with two to five basal [[bract]]s similar to the leaves but yellower. Flowering lasts from mid-spring to late summer.<ref name=blamey/><ref name=malta/>

Similar species include ''[[Euphorbia rhabdotosperma]]'', having the appearance of ''E. helioscopia'' with smaller parts and differing seed surface <ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 7 |author=Davis}}</ref> (Iran, North Caucasus, Transcaucasus, Turkey, Turkmenistan).

== Uses ==
Active ingredients extracted from ''Euphorbia helioscopia'' are used in pharmaceutical industry.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}} The plant is used in Chinese traditional medicine.<ref name=Zhang>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1248/cpb.54.1037|pmid=16819227|title=Chemical Studies on the Constituents of the Chinese Medicinal Herb Euphorbia helioscopia L|year=2006|last1=Zhang|first1=Wen|last2=Guo|first2=Yue-Wei|journal=Chemical & Pharmaceutical Bulletin|volume=54|issue=7|pages=1037–9|doi-access=free}}</ref> 

Its extract has been found to inhibit [[hepatocellular carcinoma]] ''in vivo'' in [[mice]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Hepatocellular Carcinoma Growth Is Inhibited by Euphorbia helioscopia L. Extract in Nude Mice Xenografts|vauthors=Cheng J, Han W, Wang Z, Shao Y, Wang Y, Zhang Y, Li Z, Xu X, Zhang Y |year=2015|journal=Biomed Res Int|volume=2015|pages=1–9|doi=10.1155/2015/601015|pmid=26090427|pmc=4450285|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Chemistry ==

''Euphorbia helioscopia'' contains toxic [[diterpene]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1016/0031-9422(89)80360-7|title=Diterpenes from Euphorbia helioscopia|year=1989|last1=Yamamura|first1=Shosuke|last2=Shizuri|first2=Yoshikazu|last3=Kosemura|first3=Seiji|last4=Ohtsuka|first4=Jiro|last5=Tayama|first5=Takao|last6=Ohba|first6=Shigeru|last7=Ito|first7=Masatoki|last8=Saito|first8=Yoshihiko|last9=Terada|first9=Yukimasa|journal=Phytochemistry|volume=28|issue=12|pages=3421|bibcode=1989PChem..28.3421Y }}</ref> and [[diterpene#Diterpenoids|diterpenoids]]<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1055/s-2005-837832|title=Three New Jatrophone-Type Diterpenoids from Euphorbia helioscopia|year=2005|last1=Zhang|first1=Wen|last2=Guo|first2=Yue-Wei|journal=Planta Medica|volume=71|issue=3|pages=283–6|pmid=15770554|s2cid=29332788 }}</ref> and [[phorbol esters]]. These substances are the major [[skin irritant]]s found in the plant.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1111/j.1600-0536.1980.tb05599.x|title=Skin irritants of the sun spurge (Euphorbia helioscopia L)|year=1980|last1=Schmidt|first1=Richard J.|last2=Evans|first2=Fred J.|journal=Contact Dermatitis|volume=6|issue=3|pages=204–10|pmid=7389328|s2cid=22253978}}</ref> The plant is considered poisonous when eaten raw. [[Nausea]], allergic reactions, skin irritation, vomiting  may occur after eating. <ref name="FH">{{Cite journal | last= Abid Aqsa, Mushtaq Ahmad, Muhammad Zafar, Sadia Zafar, Mohamed Fawzy Ramadan, Ashwaq T. Althobaiti, Shazia Sultana, Omer Kilic, Trobjon Makhkamov, Akramjon Yuldashev, Oybek Mamarakhimov, Khislat Khaydarov, Afat O. Mammadova, Komiljon Komilov |first= and Salman Majeed |date=December 2023|title= Foliar epidermal and trichome micromorphological diversity among poisonous plants and their taxonomic significance|journal=[[Folia Horticulturae]]|language=en|volume=35|issue=2|pages=243 – 274|doi= 10.2478/fhort-2023-0019 |issn=2083-5965|doi-access=free}}</ref>

A number of [[tannin]]s can be found in ''E. helioscopia''.<ref>{{Cite journal|doi=10.1248/cpb.38.1518|title=Tannins and related compounds. XCV. Isolation and characterization of helioscopinins and helioscopins, four new hydrolyzable tannins from Euphorbia helioscopia L. (1)|year=1990|last1=Lee|first1=Seung-Ho|last2=Tanaka|first2=Takashi|last3=Nonaka|first3=Gen-Ichiro|last4=Nishioka|first4=Itsuo|journal=Chemical & Pharmaceutical Bulletin|volume=38|issue=6|pages=1518|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Helioscopinin-A]] shows [[anti-allergic]] and [[anti-asthmatic]] activities in guinea pigs. It is suggested that this compound exerts its activities through antagonism on [[leukotriene D4]]-induced responses.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Anti-allergic and anti-asthmatic activity of helioscopinin-A, a polyphenol compound, isolated from Euphorbia helioscopia|author1=Park Kwan Ha |author2=Koh Dongsoo |author3=Lee Seungho |author4=Jung Illmin |author5=Kyung Hyun Kim |author6=Lee Chul-Hoon |author7=Kim Kye-Hoon |author8=Lim Yoongho |journal= Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology|year= 2001|volume= 11|issue= 1| pages =138–142|id= {{INIST|995613}}  }}</ref>
